card.name: Present-perfect helpers after event nouns
card.fires_on: Auxiliary or verb right after a subject in the present perfect, such as has, have, been or occurred, as in 'cases of X have been reported'. Mostly in adverse-event statements.

modes.label: Has/have after a condition
modes.description: The helper verb has or have follows a named event or condition.
modes.example: Macular edema<< has>> also been reported in patients taking fingol

modes.label: Been/occurred after have
modes.description: The participle follows has or have in a reporting phrase.
modes.example: Anaphylaxis has<< been>> observed with PEMGARDA in

modes.label: General prose
modes.description: Present-perfect or modal verbs in ordinary narrative text.

card.writes: It pushes away past-tense forms like was and came, favoring present-tense or ongoing verb forms.
card.plain: It fires on 'has' or 'have' in phrases like 'cases have been reported' and steers away from simple past tense.
